recommendations.regimenLabel: Rapidly raise glucose — oral if conscious, IV glucose or IM glucagon if not
steps: Conscious: 15–20 g fast-acting oral carbohydrate, repeat in 15 min if still low.
Impaired/NBM: IV glucose (e.g. 100 mL 20%) or IM glucagon if no IV access.
Follow with longer-acting carbohydrate once recovered.
Sulfonylurea/long-acting insulin overdose: prolonged monitoring ± octreotide; admit.
Review drugs/diabetes regimen; address recurrent causes.

drugRefs.freq: repeat after 15 min if glucose still low
drugRefs.why: First-line if the patient is conscious and able to swallow; follow with longer-acting carbohydrate once recovered.

drugRefs.dose: 100 mL of 20% (20 g); recheck and repeat as needed
drugRefs.why: For reduced consciousness or nil-by-mouth patients with IV access. 10% glucose (e.g. 150–200 mL) is an alternative.
Used when IV access is unavailable. Less effective in malnourished, alcohol-dependent or hepatic-glycogen-depleted patients, and in sulfonylurea overdose.

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Hypoglycemia
Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline — Evaluation and Management of Adult Hypoglycemic Disorders

drugRefs.freq: every 6–12 h as needed while monitoring
drugRefs.why: Suppresses sulfonylurea-driven insulin secretion and reduces recurrent hypoglycaemia; use alongside glucose with prolonged monitoring and admission.

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Hypoglycemia
Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline — Evaluation and Management of Adult Hypoglycemic Disorders

decision.label: Immediate glucose; IM glucagon if no IV access

confirm: Whipple's triad: low plasma glucose with autonomic/neuroglycopenic symptoms relieved by glucose. Identify cause (insulin/sulfonylurea, sepsis, etc.).
